highlights.message: docs: correct a stale measurement — W0b and W0d DO fire, and where they fire they are right
highlights.body:
Two lines asserted `W0b`/`W0d`/`W0g` "fire 0 times in 226 papers". Re-measured 2026-09-07
over the 101-paper corpus, pass 1, NormalizationLevel.academic, reading
NormalizationReport.steps_changed:

    W0g_dropped_minus_ci_pairing   0 papers
    W0b_minus_sign_recovery        1 paper   (efendic_2022_affect)
    W0d_minus_ci_pairing           1 paper   (efendic_2022_affect)

AND WHERE THEY FIRE THEY ARE CORRECT. Neutralising both and diffing the shipped output
recovers 62 minus signs:

    - (original: r = 2.74 [20.92, 20.30])
    + (original: r = -.74 [-0.92, -0.30])

`r = 2.74` is an impossible correlation and `[20.92, 20.30]` is a descending interval --
the genuine 2-for-U+2212 corruption, repaired properly.

This is NOT a refutation of the 226-paper figure. That figure carries no command, so it
cannot be re-run, and mine is a different corpus measured a different way -- which is
exactly why this file elsewhere says to quote a number only with the command that
regenerates it. Both lines keep their original text; the correction is appended in place
with the command that produces it.

THE OPERATIONAL POINT, and the reason this is worth a commit: `W0g` is queued for removal
(it turns `p = .05` into `p = -.05`, an impossible value, on CI containment -- which
directive 0c90a18 names verbatim as forbidden evidence). Anyone reading the "0 times" line
would reasonably sweep W0b and W0d out with it. That would LOSE real recoveries. Whether
their evidence class survives the THREE TIERS gate test is a separate owner question that
needs its own measurement -- applying one verdict to a family without testing each member
is how W0k survived the 2026-08-15 sweep, in the opposite direction.

Docs only. No behaviour change.

highlights.message: Fix zip download streaming to actually respect its own timeout
highlights.body:
.download_zip_to_cache()'s deadline check (Sys.time() > deadline) only
ran BETWEEN calls to httr2::resp_stream_raw(), never during one -- a
single stalled read defeated the timeout entirely, since
req_perform_connection()'s default blocking=TRUE mode makes that read
block indefinitely rather than returning control to the loop.

Confirmed live: a real ~65MB OSF Waterbutler zip download (326-file
repository, osf.io/wdzay) stalled mid-stream for 45+ minutes with the
underlying TCP connection sitting in CLOSE_WAIT (the remote had already
closed its side), consuming real CPU and growing memory the whole time,
with zero indication anything was wrong until the process was killed and
inspected directly.

Fixed by opening the connection with blocking=FALSE, so a zero-length
read genuinely means "no data yet" rather than blocking, and adding a
short Sys.sleep() on that branch so the loop still returns control to the
deadline check every iteration without busy-looping the CPU.

Also scales the timeout itself against the transfer's own expected size
(the sum of the selected files' sizes, already computed by every call
site to decide zip-vs-file-by-file) at a conservative 200KB/s floor,
extracted as its own testable .zip_timeout_for_size() helper -- a fixed
timeout is either too short for a large, honestly slow archive or too
long for a small stalled one to fail fast.

highlights.message: Classify genomic sequence files (FASTA/FASTQ) as data
highlights.body:
Confirmed against real corpus files (data_availability validation): a
paper whose only listed files were sequencing data in FASTA/FASTQ
format (e.g. "76_SE_0.01.fasta.gz", "thal_MK380719_TGCA.1.fq.gz") had
every one of those files fall through to "unknown", since neither
.ext_registry (data_classify_files()'s format lock) nor
metacheck::file_types (file_category()'s own lookup table) knew these
extensions -- wrongly reading such a paper as having no data available
at all, when real research data was genuinely present.

Adds the bare extensions (fasta/fa/fq/fastq) to .ext_registry and their
gzip-compressed forms (fasta.gz/fa.gz/fq.gz/fastq.gz -- the common
convention for these, since sequence files compress well) to
file_types, both as data_type "data". The compressed forms also
required a new file_category() compound-type rule (ft_has("data") &
ft_has("archive")): a name like "sample.fasta.gz" matches both its own
compound data extension and the bare "gz" extension (typed "archive"),
so its filetype comes out "data;archive" -- previously fell through to
NA for any such compound, an existing latent gap this specific,
newly-possible compound now exposed. ".dat" and a bare ".info" stay
deliberately unlocked (too generic on their own to safely classify),
so "sample.dat.gz" and similar remain "unknown" as before.

highlights.message: Fix code_read() crash on empty files and code_setwd() string-literal blindness
highlights.body:
code_read() called readr::guess_encoding() unconditionally, which returns
a zero-row result for a genuinely empty (0-byte) file; the resulting NA
encoding then crashed deep inside readr's own internals with the generic,
misleading message "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed" -- confirmed
against real 0-byte files in real GitHub repositories during the
code_check validation. A 0-byte local file now returns character(0)
directly, before guess_encoding() is ever called; file.exists() is FALSE
for a remote URL, so this leaves code_read()'s URL path unaffected.

code_setwd() had no awareness of string-literal context, so a setwd(...)
mentioned inside a string (e.g. a message() call telling a user to run
setwd() themselves) would be flagged as a live call. This reuses the same
quote-tracking approach already implemented for
.code_strip_inline_comment() (as a new, shared .code_pos_in_string()
helper) to skip a match that starts inside a string literal.

highlights.message: Fix five code_check false positives/negatives found in corpus validation
highlights.body:
Each was confirmed against real files in a 400-paper corpus (see
code_check_validation.qmd):

- Missing referenced files: the repo-listing comparison was
  case-sensitive, wrongly flagging a file that exists under a different
  letter case (e.g. code references "REM_tools.r", repo holds
  "REM_tools.R") as missing.
- Missing referenced files: vroom::vroom() was invisible to
  code_file_refs()'s R reader-keyword list (it doesn't start with
  "read"), so a missing file loaded only via vroom went undetected.
- Absolute paths: a single-segment string starting with "/" (an HTTP
  route like '/login', a paste0(var, "/eti") fragment) is now required
  to have a second path segment before matching; an all-digit UNC
  "host" (a sub()/gsub() backreference string like "\2\1") is no
  longer mistaken for \host\share.
- Comment density: a Python file documented only via docstrings read as
  0% comments with no signal that real documentation was present.
  code_line_stats() now also reports has_docstring, and the module's
  report text notes when a "no comments" file actually has one.
- Scattered library/import lines: docstring prose starting with
  "from "/"import " (Python never strips triple-quoted strings as
  comments) matched the old bare-keyword anchor, spuriously widening
  the gap between real imports and triggering a false "scattered" flag.
  The anchor now requires the full import shape.
